fix(CoA): audit the Witch Doctor class backlog — 5 fixes, 28 scenarios, 125 reports settled (#4753)

* fix(CoA/WitchDoctor): widen Overflowing Juju's classmask to reach Shadowflare's hit proc

Overflowing Juju's bonus-multiplier modifier (spell 707405) only matched
Shadowflare's DoT tick (classmask word0 bit 2, 4) via SPELLMOD_BONUS_MULTIPLIER,
so its tooltip promise to also affect the Shadowflare hit proc (ShadowflareHit,
classmask word0 bit 10, 1024) never applied. Register a GlobalScript on
GLOBALHOOK_ON_LOAD_SPELL_CUSTOM_ATTR that widens the SpellClassMask to include
both bits when the shipped DBC record still carries the narrower value, mirroring
the existing pattern used by other Ascension GlobalScripts for load-time DBC
corrections.

Fails before the fix (ShadowflareHit's own bonus multiplier is unaffected by
learning Overflowing Juju), passes after (witchdoctor-fix-overflowing-juju-shadowflare.json).

Fixes #3127

* fix(CoA/WitchDoctor): neutralize Puppeteer's Grasp's dead transform effect

Puppeteer's Grasp (707209) carries a SPELL_AURA_TRANSFORM effect whose
EffectMiscValue names a creature template that does not exist, so
HandleAuraTransform's missing-template fallback silently substitutes the
generic pig display (16358) instead of leaving the caster's own appearance
alone, contradicting the tooltip's self-only-mechanic promise (no visual
transform clause). Neutralize the dead effect slot the same way the module
already does for Shadowhunter's stray effect.

Fails before the fix (caster's display changes to the pig fallback), passes
after (witchdoctor-fix-puppeteers-grasp-transform.json).

Fixes #3114

* fix(CoA/WitchDoctor): give Amphibimorph its PvP break-on-damage and 8s duration cap

Amphibimorph's tooltip promises the transform breaks on taking damage and is
capped at 8 seconds against players, but the shipped spell carried neither
clause: AuraInterruptFlags had no TAKE_DAMAGE bit, and diminishing-returns
duration fell through to the class's generic handling instead of the fixed
8-second cap. Add the interrupt flag next to the existing Hexed pattern and
register the duration cap in GetDiminishingReturnsLimitDuration alongside the
other class-scoped fixed-duration entries already there.

Fails before the fix (breaks-on-damage and 8s PvP cap both absent), passes
after (witchdoctor-fix-934-amphibimorph-pvp-clauses.json).

Fixes #934

* fix(CoA/WitchDoctor): translate Jungle Booms' target-cap effect to a real aura

Jungle Booms' target-cap clause (705859, effect 1) shipped as a raw flat
modifier (MiscValue 34, BasePoints -4) that the generic spellmod path cannot
interpret as a max-affected-targets reduction, so the Cauldron's target count
was never actually capped. Translate it to SPELL_AURA_MOD_MAX_AFFECTED_TARGETS
scoped to the Cauldron's classmask, following the same DBC-raw-value
translation pattern already used elsewhere in ApplyContracts.

Fails before the fix (Cauldron ignores the target-cap reduction), passes
after (witchdoctor-fix-jungle-booms.json).

Fixes #2865

* fix(CoA/WitchDoctor): route the Serpent Ward's Voodoo Fire proc chance through spell mods

The Serpent Ward's proc chance for Voodoo Fire hardcoded 20/40 for
rank 1/2 without applying either rank's own SPELLMOD_CHANCE_OF_SUCCESS
modifier, so a talent or effect that raises the proc chance (Spirit
Striker) had no effect on the actual roll. Route the base chance through
ApplySpellMod keyed on the learned rank before the roll, matching how
every other spellmod-affected chance in this module is applied.

Fails before the fix (the proc-chance boost has no measurable effect on
the roll), passes after (witchdoctor-fix-spirit-striker-voodoo-fire-proc.json).

* test(CoA/WitchDoctor): correct fix-proof scenario setup for #934, #3127, #824

Live verification against slot 3 found scenario-authoring defects in three
fix-proof scenarios, none in the underlying fixes: witchdoctor-fix-934 needed
a corrected PvP-victim target setup for the transform assertion,
witchdoctor-fix-overflowing-juju needed its Bad Juju regression assertion
corrected, and witchdoctor-fix-spirit-striker needed three setup fixes
(a missing prerequisite learn step, accounting for the Serpent Ward's actual
despawn timer, and granting the Voodoo Fire rank the mechanism keys off).
All three now pass clean against the deployed fix. No C++ changed.

* test(CoA/WitchDoctor): correct regression scenario defects found in live verification

The scenario authors validated only JSON shape (no server access, per their
task rules); running all of them live against slot 3 surfaced per-scenario
authoring defects: wrong duration semantics, race conditions between casts,
DR-reset timing, melee-range fixtures, movement-interrupt mechanics, PvP
faction setup, and similar. Fixed each in place. One issue's clause
(#1363 Bwonsamdi's Edge, #1142 Fresh Ingredients, #487 Soul Marionette's
stun clause) survived repeated live testing with the correct DBC-derived
expectation and still measured wrong on the server; those three assertions
are documented and marked needs-maintainer-decision instead of forced to
pass — see decisions.md. No C++ changed; every other assertion in every
other scenario in this commit is confirmed passing against the deployed
fix/coa-witchdoctor-audit build.

refactor(CoA): make CoA a core server component (#4780)

* refactor(CoA): make CoA a required core server component

Move the vendored mod-ascension-compat module into the core tree. Its sources
become the coa static library in src/server/coa with a coa-interface include
target, its native and Python tests move to apps/coa-tests, its docs to docs/coa
and the bug-report relay to apps/coa-bugreport. modules/mod-ascension-compat keeps
the historical SQL migrations, its README and LICENSE.

The worldserver registers AddCoAScripts after the core scripts through the script
loader, so the registration order stays core, CoA, other modules. CoA configs keep
their names and install to etc/modules. The other modules include CoA headers
through coa-interface instead of relative paths, and the gameplay test driver
reaches mod-spellbook through the optional CoASpellbook provider instead of a hard
link dependency. Tooling, mechanic maps, scenarios and agent guidance follow the
new paths.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(CoA): apply CoA SQL from dbimport and keep moved files intact

- dbimport applied only the module list, so the 15 CoA migrations were skipped by
  the Docker db-import container. src/server/coa now defines COA_DATABASE_MODULE_LIST
  and COA_CONFIG_FILE_LIST once; worldserver and dbimport use them instead of the
  hand-written prefixes, and the enabled-modules list stays modules only.
- A stale modules/mod-ascension-compat/src left by an old checkout no longer turns
  the SQL directory back into a module and breaks the link.
- Moving the module dropped its .gitattributes: the byte-pinned CRLF migration lost
  its -text protection and three generated headers were normalized to LF. The
  rules now live in the root .gitattributes and the headers keep their bytes.
- The High-Risk, Bloodforged and PvP Power tests include their headers from
  src/server/coa again.
- Spellbook metrics fail with a clear message when mod-spellbook is not loaded
  instead of reporting -1, which could satisfy max or relative assertions.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(CoA): read client DBCs from the server data directory

Twenty-one CoA tests read Spell.dbc and friends from ../runtime/server/data/dbc,
a workspace layout outside the repository. They now share apps/coa-tests/client_data.py,
which reads the directory the locally installed worldserver loads, env/dist/data/dbc
(DataDir/dbc of the default acore.sh install), accepts COA_DBC_DIR to point elsewhere
and says where to put the files when they are missing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* chore(CoA): tidy the tooling that followed the move

- The dbc and mechanics suites also run when DBCStructure.h or DBCfmt.h change,
  since the Spell schema is validated against them.
- Source slices search their end marker from their start marker.
- Drop imports and a constant the path migration left unused and wrap the lines
  it pushed past 120 columns.
- The resource talent registration entry names the CoA script loader and is
  reviewed against it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(CoA): correct licensing, repository and module references

- CoA is licensed like the rest of this AzerothCore fork. Drop the MIT notice copied
  from the empty module template, whose files are all gone, and say so in the docs.
- The repository is public: remove the claims that it is private and the obsolete
  organization note, and drop the references to the separate client-kit repository.
- The historical SQL directory is described as what it is, not as a module.
- Other modules, docs and scenario contracts name CoA and its src/server/coa and
  apps/coa-tests paths instead of the removed module layout.
- Document where the CoA client DBCs belong, the module disable switch that works
  (-DMODULE_<NAME>=disabled), and keep existing comments in inherited source so
  upstream merges stay clean.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(CoA): rename the historical SQL directory to modules/mod-ascension

CoA is no longer a module, so its remaining SQL directory drops the compat name.
The migrations move unchanged; the database updater tracks applied updates by
file name and hash, so existing databases see nothing new. The CoA database module
list, the pinned-bytes rule, the gitignore whitelist, the world baseline's covered
migrations and the docs follow the new path. A stale src/ left under the old or new
name by an older checkout is still never treated as a module.

Moving applied SQL crosses the pending-SQL boundary and was explicitly requested.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(CoA): always apply CoA SQL in dbimport and check the loader call site

- dbimport applied CoA's migrations only when Updates.AllowedModules was "all".
  CoA is part of the core, so its SQL now goes to the updater with any allow-list,
  including an empty one; the list is kept alive for the loader, which holds a view.
- The registration check now also requires the worldserver to call AddCoAScripts
  exactly once, since that hand-written call replaced the generated module loader,
  and covers a second root loader definition.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* chore(CoA): read the Spell layout from DBCStructure.h again and share the DBC default

- The JSON Spell layout only existed because the inherited header had lost its field
  annotations; with those comments kept, the inspector reads them again, as on main.
  check_source keeps running the DBC suites when DBCStructure.h or DBCfmt.h change.
- The remaining seven tests that required --dbc-dir now default to the shared DBC
  directory, and an empty COA_DBC_DIR falls back to it.
- The Boost.PropertyTree check says CoA needs the headers, not only its tests.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(CoA): correct the DBC location, licensing and remaining module wording

- Say where the CoA client DBCs live without calling it the acore.sh default: Docker
  already uses env/dist/data, and a local install points DataDir there.
- State the licensing as it is: the fork is under the root GPL v2 LICENSE, most CoA
  files still carry the template's AGPL v3 notice, and changing those needs the
  contributors' agreement.
- Fix the module disable example (the variable keeps the directory's hyphens), note
  the Boost.PropertyTree requirement, restore what CoA is in its README, and drop the
  remaining private-repository claim and 'compat module' wording.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(CoA): rename the config file, keys and log categories to coa

CoA is no longer a compatibility module, so its configuration and logs drop that name:

- etc/modules/mod_ascension_compat.conf becomes coa.conf, next to coa_bugreport.conf.
- Its AscensionCompat.* keys become CoA.* in CoA, the core hooks that read them
  (CharacterHandler, WorldSocket), mod-destiny-weaver, gameplay scenarios and docs.
- CoA logs under coa, coa.gameplay_test and coa.highrisk instead of module.*;
  worldserver.conf.dist gains Logger.coa at the level module logging used.
- At startup and on config reload the worldserver logs an error while it still finds
  the old file or any AscensionCompat.* key, naming what to rename, so a server that
  was not migrated does not silently run on defaults.

docs/coa/README.md lists the upgrade steps. The item_template_ascension_compat table
keeps its name; renaming schema needs a migration of its own.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(CoA): rename item_template_ascension_compat to item_template_coa

The world table that records which item_template rows the appearance generator added
drops the compat name. A pending world update renames it only while the old table
exists and the new one does not, so a re-run, a missing table or an already renamed
database are left alone. The updater orders files by name within a pass, so on a fresh
database the applied module migration creates the table before this rename runs.

Verified on MySQL 8.4 with the real dbimport: the fresh database gets all 15 CoA
migrations, then the rename, and item_template_coa holds all 144,106 rows.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(CoA): report every unfinished step of the rename at startup

The worldserver now logs an error, naming the fix, when it still finds:
- etc/modules/mod_ascension_compat.conf, or its .dist, which acore.sh would copy
  back to the .conf; installing the server now removes the obsolete .dist;
- AscensionCompat.* config keys or AC_ASCENSION_COMPAT_* environment overrides;
- Logger.module.ascension_compat/gameplay_test/highrisk lines, or a worldserver.conf
  without Logger.coa, which would hide CoA's info and warning logs;
- the old item_template_ascension_compat table, including when a re-applied creating
  migration brings it back next to item_template_coa.

The helpers sit after the class's hooks so the overrides stay public. The upgrade
steps in docs/coa/README.md and a pending changelog entry list the same steps, and
an older pending entry no longer names AscensionCompat.LevelScaling.

Verified by starting the worldserver against a MySQL 8.4 database with each leftover
in place (all seven errors reported) and with none (no error, CoA info logs shown).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
